item.title: S&P revises Denver's outlook to negative ahead of GO sale
item.description: The competitive bond sale comes after the triple-A-rated city received a negative outlook from S&P over the use of reserves to ease budget pressures.

item.title: Munis underperform USTs after retail sales data
item.description: Tuesday was a particularly heavy day of supply at an estimated $7.5 billion, per J.P. Morgan strategists.

item.title: SMAs show growing interest in prepaid gas sector
item.description: The prepaid gas sector, once a small niche sector in the muni market, has grown exponentially over the years, with issuance reaching a record $31.4 billion in 2025.

item.title: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker calls for full pension funding goal
item.description: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker resurrected a 2024 pension proposal that would increase the state's funding goal to 100% by 2048.

item.title: Washington's $1.3 billion GO deal attracts strong investor interest
item.description: The state sold the debt in a competitive auction Tuesday morning, with interest rates landing in the low 3% to high 4% range across maturities.

item.title: States facing decoupling uncertainty
item.description: Experts looking at the oncoming effects of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act predict that states may have to raise taxes on the wealthy or corporations to compensate for rising Medicaid costs.

item.title: Sarasota Memorial Health plans bond sale
item.description: The health system plans to price $162 million on Feb. 18 and could sell up to $425 million this year.

item.title: American Dream bonds tumble
item.description: The price drops follow a lawsuit filed Friday by bondholders alleging the mall's owners colluded with the city of East Rutherford to lower the property assessment.

item.title: Former Columbus, Ohio, auditor Hugh Dorrian dies at 90
item.description: Longtime Columbus auditor Hugh Dorrian died Feb. 6. He was widely respected for his dedication to public service, transparency and timely audits.

item.title: Munis mixed, UST yields rise post-jobs report
item.description: "The bond market marked down the odds of rate cuts after the release," said FHN Financial Chief Economist Chris Low. "The fact long yields are still lower than two days ago suggests traders are skeptical of the quality of the employment data but are confident the Fed will use it as a reason to keep rates steady," he said.
